title: Crosstown Elementary Mechanical Upgrade — Phase 1
summary: A new rooftop chiller and cooling plant for an occupied downtown school, delivered around classes.
scope: New rooftop chiller on a new structural steel frame, with roofing and envelope tie-ins.
New interior mechanical room with pumps, buffer tank and chilled-water distribution.
Fan coil units, condensate drainage and controls throughout the building.
heading: Cooling for a school in the middle of downtown
overview: Crosstown Elementary sits in a dense downtown block with a rooftop deck, a planter and no street-level room for equipment. The upgrade adds mechanical cooling while the school stays open, with every heavy lift and shutdown planned around the school day.
approach: Allied leads a multi-trade team covering structural steel, roofing, cladding, framing, electrical and controls, alongside the design team and the school board. Two Sunday crane lifts were permitted with the City, including traffic management and noise exceptions. Roofing was sequenced into dry weather windows through the autumn, and temporary weather protection was checked every shift.
planning: Early structural and roofing coordination before equipment is ordered.
City street-use and crane permitting.
Phasing work around school hours, weekends and breaks.
delivery: Project management: Alex Martishyn, Project Manager.
outcome: The work is under way. This page will be updated with the completed scope once the system has been commissioned and handed over.
imageCaption: Illustrative image from the Allied mechanical services media library; project-specific photography to follow.

challenges.title: Crane lifts on a downtown street
challenges.text: The City turned down two weekend dates because of events, and fewer permits are issued in December. Allied documented the reasons for the date change and worked with the crane company until traffic management, street-use and noise-exception permits were approved for two Sunday lifts, with notices sent to residents.

challenges.title: Autumn rain over an open roof
challenges.text: The chiller lift was moved to leave a weather buffer for roofing and inspections. Temporary protection was inspected every shift, and more often in rain. Weekend roofing used dry forecast windows. A reinforced liquid-membrane detail at the steel sleepers avoided modifying the structure.

challenges.title: Design-team standards for non-mechanical trades
challenges.text: Roofing, framing, drywall and ceiling submittals each needed specialty engineer sign-off, wind-uplift calculations and warranty documents. Allied set up one submittal template and sent complete packages, which kept reviews moving.

challenges.title: An occupied school
challenges.text: Shutdowns were allowed only after hours or at weekends, and the building was a polling station on one planned date. That work was moved to another weekend.

approach: Allied resolved equipment substitutions, emergency stop and CO detection requirements through RFIs with the engineer, and scheduled after-hours electrical shutdowns. Allied also coordinates boiler startup and inspections.
planning: Boiler and controls upgrades for small schools.
Equipment selection for limited electrical service.
Startup, inspection and operator handover.

outcome: The work is under way. This page will be updated with the completed scope once the system has been commissioned and handed over.

challenges.title: Single-phase power
challenges.text: Drives were selected to take a 240V single-phase supply and run 208V three-phase pump motors, which avoided a costly service upgrade.

challenges.title: Equipment substitutions
challenges.text: Expansion tank and water meter alternates were submitted through RFIs with data sheets and approved before ordering.

challenges.title: Code items

challenges.title: After-hours shutdowns

challenges.title: Condensate drainage
